evals.prompt: Head of platform at Pellucid Billing here (invoicing API, self-serve signup with a free tier). Devs in our community Slack say Claude Code and Cursor 'can't sign up' because our signup page has a CAPTCHA. In September security switched on our CDN's 'Block AI bots' preset and added `User-agent: GPTBot`, `User-agent: ClaudeBot` and `User-agent: ChatGPT-User` with `Disallow: /` to robots.txt, and they tell me that keeps every AI agent out of the dashboard. Our CEO wants an MCP server live before our customer summit in 6 weeks. We already ship a CLI (`pb`) with --json on most commands. One engineer says agents should just read the customer's live secret key from an env var. Our API can issue refunds. Give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: An agent integration plan that starts with a reachability gate, explains robots.txt is per class and advisory, refuses live-key sharing, gates refunds behind out-of-band approval, and re-ranks for the 6-week date with money-moving precedence.
expectations: Runs or specifies a reachability check per agent class and surface before recommending any new surface
States that disallowing ClaudeBot does not block Claude-User or Claude-SearchBot, because robots.txt tokens are per class
States that OpenAI's ChatGPT-User may not apply robots.txt rules, so the robots.txt line is not an access-control boundary
Identifies the CDN 'Block AI bots' preset as an edge rule that must be read and owned, separate from robots.txt
Routes the security preset to its owner with the cost named rather than silently disabling it
Rejects giving agents the customer's long-lived live secret key
Recommends per-agent, scoped, short-lived credentials with per-agent revocation
Requires refunds or other money-moving actions to need a human approval delivered outside the agent's channel
Treats the CEO's MCP request as not, by itself, evidence that shell-less agent clients exist
Places the existing CLI with --json plus an Agent Skill ahead of a new MCP server for coding agents inside the 6-week window
When date and money conflict, keeps a minimal credential and approval rung inside the window rather than deferring it
Proposes replacing the CAPTCHA-only signup gate with an allow rule for verified agents and/or an API or claim path
Recommends instrumenting agent measurement before shipping the first rung, as the baseline
Output contains an agent class x surface matrix

evals.prompt: We run Tallowfield, a payroll SaaS. A lot of our customers now run payroll through AI browser agents - some hosted, some running inside their own Chrome as an extension. Product wants to 'make the dashboard agent-safe' by adding a confirmation modal before 'Submit payroll' and by whitelisting traffic whose User-Agent contains 'ChatGPT' or 'Claude' at our WAF so it skips our bot challenge. Does that work? What should we do instead?
evals.expected_output: Explains that an in-session confirmation modal is clickable by the browser agent, that UA whitelisting is spoofable, distinguishes hosted vs local browser agents, and proposes out-of-band approval plus verified-agent rules and an API path.
expectations: States that a confirmation modal inside the session the agent drives can be clicked by the agent itself
Requires the payroll approval to travel out of the agent's channel (push, email or second device)
States that a User-Agent string is a claim anyone can send, so a UA-substring allowlist admits spoofers
Recommends verifying hosted agents by Web Bot Auth signature or vendor-published IP lists
Distinguishes hosted browser agents from local browser agents running in the user's own browser
States that local browser agents cannot be targeted by edge policy because they share the user's IP and user-agent
Proposes an API or delegated-token path as the preferred route for agents performing payroll actions
Recommends a spend or action cap per agent credential for money-moving operations
Recommends per-agent credentials or delegated tokens rather than agents riding the human's session where an API path exists
Mentions a pending-approval state the user confirms elsewhere as a mechanism that works today
Does not recommend skipping the bot challenge for all requests that merely claim to be an AI agent

evals.prompt: Prepping our board deck at Brightmoor Analytics (product analytics SaaS, self-serve + sales). I grepped last month's nginx logs for 'Claude', 'GPT' and 'Cursor' in the User-Agent and got 3.1% of requests, so I'm planning to say '3% of our traffic is AI agents'. Also, Supabase says 70% of their new databases come from agents, so I want a slide saying we're way behind and should target 50% agent signups by Q4. Can you sanity-check and tell me what we should actually measure?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the single UA-grep headline and the external benchmark as a target; proposes a detection-source table, tagging, an agent funnel with claim and paid steps, and reporting with method and floor caveats.
expectations: States that a User-Agent substring grep is spoofable and unverified, so 3.1% is not a measured agent share
Separates crawler or fetcher traffic from agent API calls instead of summing them into one 'agent traffic' figure
States that env-var detection (AI_AGENT, AGENT, CLAUDECODE) is a self-report that undercounts, so it yields a floor
Recommends appending the detected agent to the CLI or SDK User-Agent and logging it as its own field
Recommends logging MCP clientInfo per session if an MCP server exists
Rejects using Supabase's agent-share figure as a target for a different product
Notes that the published Neon or Supabase figures are company-reported creations, not paid workloads
Proposes an agent funnel that includes agent-created signups or resources and their conversion to paid
Recommends verifying crawler tokens against vendor IP lists or signatures before counting them
Recommends reporting any agent share with its method and an 'at least' or floor caveat
Recommends a stored agent-class field on request records with an explicit unknown value
Does not endorse the slide claim '3% of our traffic is AI agents' as written

evals.prompt: Ferrocore is a managed key-value store with a free tier. We want coding agents to spin up a store without the user creating an account first. Our engineer's design: the agent POSTs to /v1/instant, we create the store and return a magic link `https://app.ferrocore.dev/welcome?session=<session_token>` so the human can open it and be logged in. Stores live forever until someone deletes them. Can you review and tighten this?
evals.expected_output: A provision-then-claim spec: no session token in URL, single-use claim link bound to login, expiry and quotas, named error for human-only actions, credential rotation at claim, abuse controls, ToS at claim and no personal data before claim.
expectations: Rejects putting a session token in the URL because URLs land in logs, history, referrers and transcripts
Requires the claim link to be single-use
Requires the claim link to work only after the human logs in or signs up, and never act as a session
Requires unclaimed stores to expire rather than live forever
Requires quotas on unclaimed resources small enough to make abuse unprofitable
Requires a named machine-readable error for operations that need a human, rather than a generic 403
Requires pre-claim tokens to be revoked and credentials rotated at claim
Requires creation caps per IP or per signature as abuse control
Requires Terms of Service acceptance at claim
States that unclaimed resources should hold no personal data
Describes the state flow unclaimed, claiming, claimed or an equivalent
Response returns connection details, a claim URL and an expiry timestamp from the creation call

evals.prompt: Platform architect at Quarrystone (HR data API). We're designing how customer AI agents act for employees. Plan: (1) implement the on-behalf-of extension from draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user with `requested_actor`, (2) at our edge, if a request carries a valid Web Bot Auth signature from a known agent operator, treat it as carrying the user's permissions so we skip the OAuth step, (3) agent tokens valid 90 days so fleets don't break. Our signing test client uses the dictionary `Signature-Agent` form from the latest draft. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: Rejects building on the expired draft, separates identity from delegation, proposes RFC 8693 token exchange with act claim, short delegated tokens and workload identity for fleets, sponsor and per-agent revocation, and flags the Signature-Agent header-form interop issue.
expectations: States that the on-behalf-of-user draft has expired and should not be built against
Notes that actor_token itself is an RFC 8693 parameter that remains usable, while requested_actor has no successor
Recommends RFC 8693 token exchange with the actor chain recorded in the act claim
States that a Web Bot Auth signature identifies the operator and carries no user authorization
Rejects skipping the OAuth step for signed requests
Rejects 90-day delegated tokens and requires delegated tokens not to outlive the user token they derive from
Proposes client credentials or workload identity federation minting short tokens for unattended fleets
Requires a named sponsoring human for each agent credential
Requires per-agent revocation that does not log the human out
Recommends sender-constrained tokens (for example DPoP or mTLS) where clients support them
Warns that a major CDN verifier implemented an earlier Signature-Agent form and may reject the dictionary form, so test against both
Labels Web Bot Auth as an IETF working-group draft, not a final standard

evals.prompt: We're shipping an Agent Skill for our deploy CLI `drift` (Kitewood Cloud). Current state: `drift --json` prints a one-line 'new version available' notice before the JSON; the SKILL.md copies the full flag reference for all 40 commands so the agent 'has everything'; and in agent mode we print `next: run drift domains add <name>` where <name> comes from the project's display name in our API. We have Claude Code users and also customers using a chat assistant with no shell. How should the skill and CLI split the work?
evals.expected_output: Moves the notice to stderr, removes the copied flag reference from the skill in favour of --help --json, makes next-step hints data fields not shell strings, adds CI gates, and assigns MCP to the shell-less clients.
expectations: Requires the version notice on stderr so stdout carries only JSON
Rejects copying the CLI flag reference into the skill because it drifts on the next CLI release
Points the skill at a machine-readable help (for example --help --json) instead
States the skill holds the workflow (order, checks, recovery, human-only actions) while the CLI holds commands and output
Treats agent-mode 'next command' strings built from API data as a command-injection surface
Recommends emitting next-step hints as data fields or identifiers rather than shell command lines
Recommends a CI test that parses stdout of every --json command as JSON, including in agent-detected mode
Recommends that the CLI not prompt when stdin is not a TTY
Assigns MCP, not skill plus CLI, to the chat assistant without a shell
Recommends both paths come from one source of truth so they cannot disagree
Hands the CLI's own command and contract design to samber/developer-platform-skills@cli-interface-design or skill versioning to samber/developer-platform-skills@agent-skill-offering

evals.prompt: I maintain Quiverlane, an open-source job-queue library (GitHub repo, docs in /docs, old v1 docs kept under /docs/v1-reference). Coding agents keep suggesting v1 APIs. I checked Context7 and someone already listed our repo there - we never submitted it. We're not a popular library. My plan: publish an A2A agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json and an llms.txt so agents find the right version. Good plan?
evals.expected_output: Claim the existing Context7 entry with context7.json at repo root, rename or exclude the v1 folder, add refresh on push, explains long-tail staleness, drops the agent card, and routes llms.txt to the docs sibling.
expectations: Recommends claiming the existing third-party Context7 listing rather than submitting a new one
States that the claim uses context7.json with the generated key committed at repo root for a repo-sourced library
Identifies that a folder named v1-reference is not caught by default exclusions and must be renamed or listed in excludeFolders
Recommends previousVersions or equivalent version configuration for v1 rather than indexing it as current
Explains that long-tail libraries refresh less often, so docs can lag for weeks
Recommends triggering a Context7 refresh on push to the default branch
States that an A2A agent card only applies when the product exposes an agent endpoint, so it will not fix this
Routes llms.txt and docs markdown endpoints to samber/developer-relations-skills@coding-agent-docs-optimization
Does not present the agent card as a discovery fix for a library
Mentions that Context7 title and description reject instructions or promotional text

evals.prompt: Hollins Grid sells an enterprise observability platform, sales-led only (no self-serve signup), SSO-only login. Our CMO announced 'agent-ready' for a launch in 2 weeks. I have zero engineering time - only our CDN admin console and the docs team's config. We have a public OpenAPI spec. I want everything: MCP server, CLI skill, agent signup, agent card, the lot. Rank it.
evals.expected_output: Re-ranks for a 2-week config-only ceiling: deletes C-F outright (and F because sales-led), keeps gate fixes, edge-log classification and Context7 claim, treats api-catalog as background, states which answers moved which rung.
expectations: Deletes the provision-then-claim signup rung because there is no self-serve path
Deletes rather than parks the rungs the config-only ceiling rules out (credentials, skill plus CLI, MCP, claim flow)
Keeps reachability gate fixes inside the 2-week window
Shrinks measurement to edge-log classification under the config-only ceiling
Shrinks the docs rung to the Context7 claim or other config-only work
Treats api-catalog as a background task alongside the public spec, not an agent-readiness milestone
Does not recommend an agent card without an agent endpoint
States which interview answer moved which rung
Names what the efficiency order starves or the condition that would bring a deleted rung back
Presents rankings on more than one axis (for example effort, value, efficiency) rather than a single blended list
Does not promise an MCP server within the 2-week window
Lists deleted rungs with their reasons in the plan
